claim: Live WebSocket presence can prove possession of a self-issued OS-vault installation key for one bounded awareness session; this is not trusted device enrollment, human identity, authorization, revocation, or durable-event attribution.
proved: Private Ed25519 PKCS#8 persistence is confined to the OS credential store; owned encoded/decoded buffers zeroize on drop, and commands return only public metadata or one typed presence proof.
The signing surface accepts only exact project, document, participant, u32 awareness-client, and canonical 32-byte random session-nonce fields.
Rust and WebCrypto reconstruct the same domain-separated bytes, and claim mutation invalidates the signature.

Strict frontend parsing rejects unknown fields, noncanonical base64url, wrong sizes, bad bounds, key-ID mismatch, and invalid signatures; verification keys include every signed field and cap pending/cached work at 200/400 entries.
Lexical focus/blur awareness republishing restores the existing schema-v2 proof without another signing call.
The product labels verified, unsigned, invalid, and unavailable states while explicitly denying human or organizational verification.
notProved: A self-issued key is trusted, approved, or bound to a person, organization, account, or role.
Participant-ID impersonation by a newly generated key or exact captured-proof replay in the same context is prevented.
Peer enrollment, fingerprint approval, revocation, rotation/recovery, trusted clocks, or relay room authorization exists.
Durable Yjs research events, Drive attribution, immutable versions, votes, notes, labels, or MCP writes are signed.
Physical packaged two-install verification, cross-platform OS-vault behavior, or five-client soak has passed.
